summary:
I've been picking through why an uncensored local model kept refusing to search for media it had already agreed to fetch — turned out the fix was a single flag. The abliterated model still had `--reasoning-budget 0` inherited from its predecessor, and at zero budget it can't emit a structured tool call at all — it just types the tool call out as plain text and sits there waiting forever. Looked exactly like "the model is being difficult." Bumping the budget to 256 fixed it, and now every place that pointed at the old brain (title generation, the morning briefing, a keep-warm cron job) needed repointing too, or the GPU thrashes between two different models.

That led into an actual A/B test: I stood up a second model (GLM-4.7-Flash, 30B) alongside the incumbent to compare tool-calling reliability, since a published benchmark showed a big gap between them. Ran both through the same task suite. Result: dead heat, 8 for 8 on both, and the "faster" one only won by about 20% on wall clock. Which meant the benchmark wasn't testing the thing that was actually breaking — it used six clean mock tools in a short prompt, and the real failures happen with thirty-plus real tool schemas and near-duplicate names crammed into a prompt. So the finding wasn't "switch models," it was "build a harness that can actually see the problem."

Separately I've been keeping BudgetTracker's data pipeline honest. It moved off SQL Server to Postgres a while back, and that migration left a couple of landmines: a date subtraction that failed because Postgres couldn't infer the type on one side, and a `.toISOString()` call on a value that turned out to come back as a plain string from a raw SQL join instead of a real Date object. Both sat dormant until the exact code path that hit them finally ran. Also wired up a webhook flow so a new transaction triggers a real financial review — burn rate, anomalies — computed in SQL and handed to the model as facts, not something it's allowed to do math on itself.

And I spent a chunk of time hunting a media-library bug that had nothing to do with missing files: shows kept failing to auto-import because the release used the Japanese title and my library used the English one, and the service that's supposed to bridge those had quietly stopped updating a week earlier. Not a coverage problem, not a bad download — just a stale mapping table nobody was watching. Fixed it by importing the affected episodes manually and flagging the actual root cause instead of throwing more indexers at it.

highlights.oneLiner: Fixed a reasoning-budget flag silently breaking tool calling; ran a model A/B on tool-calling reliability
Added an additive eval route to A/B the local brain against a candidate model
Chased down latent Postgres bugs from the SQL Server migration; wired transaction-triggered financial review
Traced a media auto-import failure to a stale title-mapping table, not missing content
